messages:
maria: Quick sync — I put together a concise launch checklist for the model-variant gating feature. Goal = let requests failover automatically to compatible variants across tiers/regions while preserving latency SLOs. Posting acceptance criteria + edge cases we need decisions on.

dave: Ack. Can you highlight the minimum telemetry we need to consider gating safe?

maria: Sure. Core acceptance criteria (draft):
- G1: Canary rollouts must serve <= 1% of traffic for 24h with no P0 customer impact.
- G2: Automated fallback triggers when 5xx rate for a variant > 0.5% over 5m AND tail latency (p95) increases > 2x baseline.
- G3: Region affinity respected: requests pinned to region where customer opted in; fallback to cross-region only if latency delta < 150ms and customer allows.
- G4: Model compatibility matrix enforced: only variants marked compatible in catalog can be chosen for fallback.
- G5: Metrics emitted per-request: variant_id, tier, region, routing_decision, reason_code.

anika: For G2, 0.5% seems tight for high-volume routes. Suggest metric window = 5m and require sustained increase over 2 windows (10m) for auto-fallback.

maria: Good point. Proposal: require both conditions — error rate > 0.5% for 10m and p95 > 2x baseline for 5m. That reduces churn. Anyone opposed?

raj: No objection. Need to call out cold-start spikes for dedicated capacity — we should ignore spikes during node scale events. Add a suppressor when scaling=true.

kate: Also need telemetry tag for scale_state to filter those events.

maria: Added: telemetry includes scale_state.

maria: Draft runbook snippet for on-call when fallback is triggered:
- Alert: variant_fallback_autoactivated (severity=warning) -> message: variant X fallback to Y in region Z.
- Runbook: check `variant_errors{variant="X",region="Z"}` and `node_scale_state{region="Z"}`; if scale_state==true, annotate and wait 10m; otherwise escalate.

deploy-bot: deploy started: gating-service:v2.3.1 -> staging at 2024-06-12T17:40:00Z

dave: For launch we need an e2e test harness that simulates mixed tiers (free, standard, enterprise) and cross-region fallbacks. Who owns that?

anika: I can take the harness. Plan: deterministic replay + injected latency/failure scenarios. Will add tests for model-compatibility mismatch.

maria: Owner list (w/ deadlines):
- E2E harness: anika — PR by 1715100000 (one week).
- Catalog compatibility API + UI flags: dave — PR by 1715090000.
- Telemetry + metrics: raj — PR by 1715095000.
- Runbooks & ops playbook: kate + opsbot — draft by 1715096000.

kate: Ops checklist: add a manual rollback API that can pin customer to previous model variant (per-customer override). Must be available before GA.

maria: Agreed. That counts as a hard launch gate.

maria: Edge cases we need to document explicitly:
1) Variant config says "compatible" but quantization causes answer drift — require canary evaluation against a small prompt-set (golden prompts) and monitor quality degradation (BLEU/embedding-similarity).
2) Customer with strict data residency — never cross-region fallback; must fail closed and return 503 with clear reason_code=DATA_RESIDENCY_BLOCK.
3) Multi-model requests (hybrid pipelines) where different steps prefer different variants — route each step independently but surface an overall routing_decision summary.

raj: For #1, add metric quality_regression_ratio and require threshold < 2% on golden prompt-set during canary. If exceeded, block rollout.

maria: Noted. Also calling out performance budget per tier (simple targets):
- free: p95 <= 1.2s, canary traffic max 0.5%
- standard: p95 <= 0.6s, canary traffic max 1%
- enterprise: p95 <= 0.3s, canary traffic max 2%

dave: Those budgets mirror current infra SLAs, ok. Need to surface these in Console per-model so devs can opt-in.

maria: UX note: Console must show compatibility reasons when a variant is excluded (e.g., "quantized-only", "diff-arch", "region-mismatch"). Add as acceptance criteria for Catalog UI.

opsbot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance tomorrow 2024-06-13 02:00-03:00 UTC — suppress auto-fallback alerts during window? react with :warning: if yes.

kate: Yes please suppress for maintenance window. We'll still emit events but mark them maintenance=true.

maria: Final ask before I turn this into a PRD: any customer-driven asks we should escalate? Acme asked for guaranteed cross-region fallback latency < 100ms — that's likely unrealistic globally. Suggest we offer a dedicated reserved pool in target region for Enterprise customers as workaround. Thoughts?

dave: Agree. Offer dedicated pool + negotiated SLA as enterprise offering. Don't bake that into default auto-fallback logic.

anika: Ok, will add a test case for reserved pool scenarios.

maria: Thanks all. I'll convert this thread into PRD draft and tag owners. If no blockers, target doc PR tomorrow EOD. :thumbsup:

kate: LGTM

maria: Filing PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/312 — feedback welcome.
